body.hook: Tacos, paella, empanadas, arepas: food is one of the best ways to explore Spanish-speaking cultures. Every country has its own dishes and even its own words for the same food. Today you'll learn to talk about food and say what you like and don't like.

vocabulary.term: el desayuno / el almuerzo / la cena

study.title: ¿Qué te gusta comer?
study.question: How do I talk about food I like and don't like?
study.passage:
Food vocabulary: la manzana (apple), el plátano (banana), el pan (bread), el queso (cheese), el pollo (chicken), el arroz (rice), los frijoles (beans), la ensalada (salad), la sopa (soup), los huevos (eggs), la leche (milk), el jugo (juice; "el zumo" in Spain), el agua (water).
Gustar works differently from "to like." It means "to be pleasing to":
• Me gusta el pan. (Bread is pleasing to me = I like bread.)
• Me gustan las manzanas. (Apples are pleasing to me = I like apples.) Use gustan when the food is plural.
• No me gusta la sopa. (I don't like soup.)
• ¿Te gusta el queso? (Do you like cheese?)
Dialogue:
Lucía: ¿Qué te gusta comer en el desayuno?
Mateo: Me gustan los huevos y el pan. ¿Y a ti?
Lucía: A mí me gusta la fruta, especialmente los plátanos. No me gusta el café.
Mateo: ¿Te gusta la comida mexicana?
Lucía: ¡Sí! Me gustan mucho los tacos. Son deliciosos.
English support: ¿Y a ti? = And you? A mí me gusta = I like (emphasis). especialmente = especially. mucho = a lot.
Activity: Survey: ask five classmates "¿Te gusta…?" about four foods and record "sí" or "no." Report one result: "A tres estudiantes les gusta la pizza."
study.source: Original dialogue written for this lesson.

body.hook: In Spanish you don't say "I like pizza." You say "Me gusta la pizza," which really means "Pizza is pleasing to me." It looks backwards at first, but once it clicks, you can talk about anything you like.

vocabulary.definition: I like… (one thing or an activity)

study.title: ¿Te gusta?
study.question: How do I talk about what I like with gustar?
study.passage:
Gustar guide (written for this lesson):
Gustar agrees with the thing liked, not the person: Me gusta la pizza (one thing). Me gustan las fresas (plural). Me gusta bailar (activities use gusta).
Who likes it: me (me), te (you), le (him/her/you formal), nos (us), les (them). Le gusta el chocolate. Nos gustan los tacos.
Use the article: Me gusta el queso (not "me gusta queso").
Degrees: Me encanta(n) (I love) > Me gusta(n) mucho > Me gusta(n) > No me gusta(n) mucho > No me gusta(n) nada (I don't like at all).
Reactions: A mí también (me too, after a positive). A mí tampoco (me neither, after a negative). A mí no / A mí sí (I don't / I do).
Activity: food survey: ¿Te gusta el brócoli? ¿Te gustan las papas fritas? Record answers and report with le gusta / le gustan.
study.source: Original activity written for this lesson.

body.objective: Students will be able to order in a restaurant.
body.iCan: I can order in a restaurant.
successCriteria: I can order food politely with quisiera
I can ask questions about the menu and prices
I can role-play a restaurant conversation
body.hook: "¡Buen provecho!" In restaurants from Mexico City to Madrid, ordering politely and asking for the bill are the skills you'll use most. Today you'll eat, at least in a role-play.

study.title: En el restaurante
study.question: How do I order in a restaurant in Spanish?
study.passage:
Dialogue (read in threes):
Camarero: Buenas tardes. ¿Qué desean?
Ana: Buenas tardes. Para mí, una ensalada y una quesadilla, por favor.
Leo: Quisiera los tacos de pollo y un agua de jamaica.
Camarero: ¿Y para beber, señorita?
Ana: Un jugo de naranja, por favor.
(más tarde) Camarero: ¿Algo más? ¿Un postre?
Leo: ¿Cuánto cuesta el flan?
Camarero: Cuesta cuatro dólares.
Leo: Sí, un flan, por favor.
Ana: La cuenta, por favor.
Menu (Restaurante Sol, in dollars): ensalada 6; quesadilla 8; tacos de pollo 10; enchiladas 11; agua de jamaica (hibiscus drink) 3; jugo de naranja 3; flan 4; churros 5.
Culture: agua de jamaica is a popular hibiscus drink in Mexico; flan is a caramel custard dessert; in many Spanish-speaking countries you must ask for the bill, because the server won't bring it until you do.
Activity: role-play in threes; the server totals the bill.
study.source: Original dialogue and menu written for this lesson.
discussion: Why use quisiera instead of quiero?
Why do you need to ask for the bill?
study.product: Perform a restaurant role-play with six polite phrases, and write the order and total bill.
